name: Traffic Signaling
summary: Adversaries may use traffic signaling to hide open ports or other malicious functionality used for persistence or command and control. Traffic signaling involves the use of a magic value or sequence that must be sent to a system to trigger a special response, such as opening a closed port or executing a malicious task. strategies.name: Traffic Signaling (Port-knock / magic-packet → firewall or service activation) – T1205

analytics.name: Analytic 1448
analytics.guidance: A remote host sends a short sequence of failed connection attempts (RST/ICMP unreachable) to a set of closed ports. Within a brief window the endpoint (a) adds/enables a firewall rule or (b) a sniffer-backed process begins listening or opens a new socket, after which a successful connection occurs. Also detects Wake-on-LAN magic packets seen on local segment.

analytics.name: Analytic 1449
analytics.guidance: Closed-port knock sequence from a remote IP followed by on-host firewall change (iptables/nftables) or daemon starts listening (socket open) and a successful TCP/UDP connect. Optional detection of libpcap/raw-socket sniffers spawning to watch for secret values.

analytics.name: Analytic 1450
analytics.guidance: Remote knock sequence followed by PF/socketfilterfw rule update or a background process listening on a new port; then a successful TCP session. Also flags WoL magic packets on local segment.

analytics.name: Analytic 1451
analytics.guidance: Crafted ‘synful knock’ patterns toward routers/switches (same src hits interface/broadcast/network address on same port in short order) followed by ACL/telnet/SSH enablement or module change. Detect device image/ACL updates then a new mgmt session.
